title: Mayo Clinic AI-ECG flags low ejection fraction at 97.88%; 41-year-old treated, EF recovers to 55%
summary: At Mayo Clinic two ECGs scored 97.88% and 98.67% for reduced ejection fraction in a 41-year-old with no cardiac history; echo confirmed HFrEF, therapy followed, EF 55% at 4 months. Developer-authored.
account: Harmon, Witt, Friedman and Attia (Cardiovascular Digital Health Journal, 24 August 2021) report a 41-year-old man with class III obesity, sleep apnea, no cardiac history. Two electrocardiograms (ECGs) on Mayo's AI-ECG dashboard gave reduced-ejection-fraction probabilities of 97.88% and 98.67%. Echocardiography next day confirmed reduced function. Guideline-directed therapy for new heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) began. At four months his ejection fraction had risen to 55%, attributed by the authors to therapy, recovery from post-viral sequelae and weight loss. All four authors are at Mayo Clinic, which developed the algorithm and licensed it to Eko and Anumana. Friedman, Attia and other inventors may receive financial benefit. The same group published further cases. Dhawan et al. (PACE, 2024): AI-ECGs predicting left-bundle-branch-block cardiomyopathy six years before presentation. Kenyon et al. (J Pers Med, 2024): AI-ECG prompting an early AL amyloidosis diagnosis. Liu et al. (HeartRhythm Case Reports, 2025): defibrillator decision-making. No source outside Mayo was found for these cases.
purpose: Screen 12-lead ECGs for a low left-ventricular ejection fraction with a convolutional neural network
system: Mayo Clinic AI-ECG low-ejection-fraction algorithm (AI-ECG dashboard)
developer: Mayo Clinic (licensed to Eko and Anumana)
segment: Adults presenting with unexplained symptoms and an ECG

ratings.reason: New HFrEF identified and treated; ejection fraction 55% at four months.

comparator.against: the conventional reading of the same ECGs, which showed only nonspecific abnormalities

comparator.after: high probabilities of reduced ejection fraction (97.88% and 98.67%); at a 4-month follow-up visit, the patient had improved left ventricular ejection fraction to 55%

later.note: The Mayo-developed low-ejection-fraction algorithm, licensed to Eko Health and trained on Mayo's ECG dataset, received FDA clearance in early April 2024 for use with Eko's digital stethoscopes, and Mayo authors continued to publish AI-ECG case reports through 2025.
later.quote: Eko Health received FDA clearance this week for a new AI-powered tool that aids in the early detection of low ejection fraction

fields.account: Harmon, Witt, Friedman and Attia (Cardiovascular Digital Health Journal, 24 August 2021) report a 41-year-old man with class III obesity, sleep apnea, no cardiac history. Two electrocardiograms (ECGs) on Mayo's AI-ECG dashboard gave reduced-ejection-fraction probabilities of 97.88% and 98.67%. Echocardiography next day confirmed reduced function. Guideline-directed therapy for new heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) began. At four months his ejection fraction had risen to 55%, attributed by the authors to therapy, recovery from post-viral sequelae and weight loss. All four authors are at Mayo Clinic, which developed the algorithm and licensed it to Eko and Anumana. Friedman, Attia and other inventors may receive financial benefit. The same group published further cases. Dhawan et al. (PACE, 2024): AI-ECGs predicting left-bundle-branch-block cardiomyopathy six years before presentation. Kenyon et al. (J Pers Med, 2024): AI-ECG prompting an early AL amyloidosis diagnosis. Liu et al. (HeartRhythm Case Reports, 2025): defibrillator decision-making. No source outside Mayo was found for these cases.
